The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}({a}_{i}-1)({b}_{j}+1) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}({a}_{i}-1){\sum }_{j=1}^{20}({b}_{j}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}({a}_{i}-1){\sum }_{j=1}^{20}({b}_{j}+1) & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{a}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}1)\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{20}{b}_{j}+{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}1) \\  & =(12-10)\cdot (5+20) \\  & =(2)\cdot (25) \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$
